title: Drishyam 3 Just Became the First South Indian Film of 2026 to Cross $10 Million Overseas. Mohanlal's Franchise Is Now a Global Event.
excerpt: The Malayalam original has earned nearly ₹80 crore gross in India in six days, with Kerala alone contributing ₹51 crore. The Ajay Devgn Hindi version hasn't even released yet.
body:
Six days into its theatrical run, **Drishyam 3** — the Malayalam original starring Mohanlal — has crossed the $10 million mark in overseas markets, making it the first South Indian film of 2026 to reach that milestone. The number is significant not just for what it says about this particular film, but for what it reveals about where Malayalam cinema stands in the global market.

## The Numbers

The film's India net collection after six days stands at ₹68.60 crore, with a total India gross of ₹79.62 crore. The Malayalam version is doing the heavy lifting, contributing ₹59.05 crore in net collections — making it the second-highest six-day total in Mollywood history, behind only **L2: Empuraan**.

Kerala remains the engine: ₹50.95 crore gross in six days, the second-fastest film to reach the ₹50 crore mark in the state (after *L2: Empuraan*, which did it in five). Karnataka has added ₹10.28 crore, with Andhra Pradesh–Telangana at ₹7 crore and Tamil Nadu at ₹6.35 crore.

The overseas performance is where the diaspora story lives. The $10 million mark — achieved faster than any South Indian film this year — reflects the growing economic power of Malayali communities in the Gulf, the US, the UK, Canada, and Australia. The Gulf market in particular has been a traditional stronghold for Malayalam cinema, and Drishyam 3 is capitalising on that base while expanding into Western territories that the franchise's reputation has prised open.

## Why This Franchise Travels

The Drishyam franchise has always been about something more than the mystery at its centre. Georgekutty's story — an ordinary man who outsmarts the system to protect his family — resonates universally, but it hits a specific nerve in diaspora communities where the feeling of being an outsider navigating unfamiliar systems is a daily reality.

Mohanlal's performance anchors the franchise's emotional architecture. He plays Georgekutty not as a hero but as a father — resourceful, morally ambiguous, and deeply human. That portrayal has earned the franchise fans far beyond the Malayalam-speaking world. The Hindi remake (with Ajay Devgn) grossed over ₹300 crore combined for its two instalments. The Telugu, Tamil, and Kannada versions have found their own audiences.

Now, with the third instalment, the Malayalam original is proving that it doesn't need the Hindi market to achieve global scale.

## The Hindi Version Is Coming

The Ajay Devgn-led **Drishyam 3** (Hindi) recently completed its shoot, with director Abhishek Pathak sharing a heartfelt wrap-up post. The film also stars Jaideep Ahlawat, who played a memorable role in the second instalment. The Hindi version is expected to release later this year, and its box office performance will inevitably be compared to the Malayalam original.

But here's the shift: the conversation used to be about whether the Hindi remake could match the original. Now the question is whether the original needs a Hindi remake at all. The answer, based on the $10 million overseas figure, is complicated. The remake expands the IP's reach into the massive Hindi-belt market, but the original is increasingly capable of standing on its own in the very markets where Hindi films traditionally dominated.

## What It Means for Malayalam Cinema

This $10 million milestone is part of a larger trend. **L2: Empuraan**, **Thudarum**, and **Vaazha 2** have all performed strongly in 2026, but Drishyam 3's overseas number is the clearest signal yet that Malayalam cinema has built a durable international audience. It's not one-off viral hits anymore — it's a pipeline.

For NRIs, particularly the Malayali diaspora but increasingly South Indian audiences of all backgrounds, these films are cultural events. They're what you see on opening weekend, what you discuss at community gatherings, what you send clips of to family back home. Drishyam 3 isn't just a box office success. It's proof that a Malayalam-language film about a family in Kerala can fill theatres in Houston, London, and Sydney on a Tuesday afternoon.

The franchise shows no signs of slowing down. Georgekutty's story isn't over. And neither is Malayalam cinema's global moment.

*Sources: SacNilk, Bollywood Hungama, Box Office India*
